payload.feature:
Decision 0035 is accepted (ruled 2026-09-03; docs/decisions/0035-effort-is-part-of-the-hire.md). Enact it. Read the decision first: each of its seven rulings names an enforcement binding, and those bindings are this commission — nothing beyond them.

What to build:

1. contracts/seat-record.v2.schema.json beside v1, and v1 is never edited (ruling 7). v2 adds `effort` to the per-turn checkpoint, the finishing checkpoint and the successful result, described as configuration, never as a report; and `reasoning_output_tokens`, a reported subset of `output_tokens` the way `cache_read_tokens` is a subset of `input_tokens`, never added to a total a second time, absent where a harness reports no per-turn figure — never zero, never back-filled from the run total. Records validate against the version their run's engine wrote (brokkr-store validator). Add the v2 row to contracts/README.md and pin v2 in crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/frozen_contracts.rs beside v1.

2. The built-in folds in brokkr-protocol::adapters and their conformance shims (ruling 3, ruling 4). codex: `effort` per turn from the thread record's turn_context.effort through the decision 0032 locator; `reasoning_output_tokens` per turn from turn.completed.usage; and map the `cache_write_input_tokens` it already receives onto the `cache_write_tokens` v1 defines. claude: `effort` from the harness's own echo beside each assistant record; reasoning only in its result (output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens), so per-turn stays absent. dsh: `effort` is the 0031 sentinel `not reported` — the lanes carry a real control but nothing echoes it. exec: `not applicable`. Driver conformance covers every built-in driver.

3. Every model pin carries an effort pin (ruling 5). Where decision 0031 ruling 2 requires a concrete model, an effort-bearing driver (claude, codex, dsh) also requires a concrete effort, in the vocabulary that driver's adapter declares; exec needs none. In the agent library each `models` candidate gains a companion effort, so a charter names the effort it hires as it names the model. Bundle compilation scans the fully composed seat tree and reports every unpinned seat, member and step in one refusal beside the existing model refusal, with the repair; `brokkr doctor --bundle` exposes the same refusal. Then pin an effort in every shipped agent, bundle and recipe so that all of bundles/self, bundles/verify and recipes/* compile: their digests move, and that is the identity change ruling 5 intends — re-pin the witnesses in crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/witness_digests.rs and crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/compose_tests.rs, and say why in the commit. Choose each effort as the plainest reading of what the seat does today (the driver's default where a default exists); do not tune.

4. brokkr-view derives the pin and the applied effort as separate cells, both labelled configuration, and old-journal absence stays absent with no fallback (ruling 6). Reasoning sums exactly as documented: extend docs/guides/driver-authoring.md with the sum rules, the v2 fields, and the sentence ruling 2 asks for — `model` is the provider's claim, not proof — and mirror that wording in every readout that labels the field (brokkr costs, brokkr inspect, the tui).

Do not touch: the wire protocol (forge-driver/v1 — effort and reasoning are additive payload facts, like model before them), any journal row, any frozen evaluator fixture, seat-record v1, or the dsh headless profile (its thin record is a finding the decision deliberately leaves unruled). Full gate as the verify seat knows it, exact coverage included; every new refusal has a test that trips it.

result.notes: Framed decision 0035's enactment: seat-record v2 beside the frozen v1 (effort + reasoning_output_tokens), the codex/claude/dsh/exec folds and conformance, an effort-pin compile refusal beside the model-pin one plus repin of every shipped agent/bundle/recipe and the two witness-digest test files, and the brokkr-view/doctor/driver-authoring.md readout updates. Task file names concrete files (adapters.rs fold functions, bundle.rs enforce_model_pins/enforce_model_policy, seat_record.rs validator, witness_digests.rs WITNESSES array) and the coherent-but-open design question (how a record's target schema version is known at validation time). Request is coherent and does not violate any frozen contract as framed.

Compile reports every unpinned seat/member/step in one refusal beside the model refusal with the repair, and doctor --bundle exposes it. All 11 shipped bundles and recipes compile; the 8 witness and 5 uncomposed digests moved and the tests say why.

(4) brokkr-view carries the pin and the applied effort as two cells, neither filled from the other, old-journal absence visible on both; the engine journals the pin additively beside the model. driver-authoring.md gained the full sum-rule table, the v2 fields, and ruling 2's sentence ('model is the provider's claim, not proof'), mirrored in brokkr costs, brokkr inspect, the terminal readout and the tui.

Commission coverage checked and confirmed: contracts/seat-record.v1.schema.json has zero diff and its embedded byte-pin test is unchanged; v2 lands beside it as a strict superset (optional properties only) with effort described as configuration and reasoning_output_tokens as a never-re-added subset, absent rather than zero; the contracts/README.md row and the frozen_contracts.rs v2 presence pin are both there; version dispatch keys on the run/started manifest engine string, defaults to v1 when absent or unparseable, and is exercised both ways over one record. Folds: codex reads turn_context.effort through the 0032 locator and reports reasoning per turn plus the previously-dropped cache_write_input_tokens -> cache_write_tokens; claude reads its per-record echo and keeps per-turn reasoning absent with thinking_tokens only on the result; dsh writes 'not reported'; exec writes 'not applicable'. Driver conformance covers all five built-ins including the absence and sentinel cases and now validates against V2. Ruling 5's refusals all exist and all have tests that trip them (inline unpinned effort, agent candidate pinning none, level outside the declared vocabulary, agent pinning an effort against an effort_flag:unsupported provider, efforts naming a candidate outside the chain, exec exempt), and doctor --bundle exposes the compile refusal. resolve() returns Err on ANY chain entry's gap, so an unpinned candidate cannot silently downgrade to the next one. brokkr-view carries pin and applied as two cells with no fallback either way, VIEW_VERSION bumped to 7, reasoning never enters total_tokens in finish_usage / usage_text / compare.rs. Digests re-pinned in both witness_digests.rs (8) and compose_tests.rs (5 + 1 composed golden), each with prose saying the effort pin is why. Non-goals held: no diff under fixtures/, reference/, policy/, specs/, openspec/, no driver-protocol contract change, no journal row rewritten, dsh headless profile untouched. claude --help on this machine confirms '--effort <level> (low, medium, high, xhigh, max)', matching adapters/claude.json exactly.

I applied no fixes. Four low findings and one info remain:

1. LOW (correctness / commission completeness) — crates/brokkr-cli/src/render.rs:410-424. Ruling 2's binding is 'how the model field is described in docs/guides/driver-authoring.md and in every readout that labels it', and the task named brokkr costs, brokkr inspect and the tui. The tui got it (tui.rs:2881 renders 'model <x> (claimed)'). brokkr inspect got only a source comment: its seats table still has a bare 'model' column and the new detail line reads 'effort pinned X · applied Y (configuration)' with nothing about the model being a claim. brokkr costs is JSON, where a prose qualifier has no place, so the comment there is defensible. The commit message's 'Every readout that labels the field now says so' overstates it for inspect. Repair: one legend/qualifier line in seats_block plus the two render/tests.rs goldens.

2. LOW (correctness) — crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs, CodexThreadEcho::locate, called only from the 'thread.started' arm (~line 583). The thread-record path is resolved exactly once and cached as Option<PathBuf>; if codex has not yet filed the rollout at the instant it announces the thread, path stays None for the life of the seat and effort() returns None on every turn, so the record says 'not reported' for a codex seat. That is dsh's sentinel, and ruling 3 makes the distinction between the two sentinels load-bearing — a codex seat would be indistinguishable from a harness that echoes nothing. The conformance shim writes the thread file BEFORE printing thread.started, so no test can trip this ordering. Repair: have effort() re-locate lazily while path is None.

3. LOW (security) — crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs, find_codex_thread: the match is `name.ends_with(".jsonl") && name.contains(thread_id)`, and thread_id arrives unvalidated from the codex stream (plain_thread_id guards only the resume argv path, not locate). A degenerate id — a single character, say — matches an arbitrary file anywhere in the bounded walk under $CODEX_HOME/sessions, so a concurrent or historical seat's thread can lend this one its effort. That is precisely what the function's own doc comment says must not happen ('found by the thread id codex itself announced, never by the newest file'). No path component is derived from thread_id, so there is no traversal, and the value read is clamped to one bounded word and nothing executable is derived from it — the impact is a false configuration fact in an append-only journal, not code execution, which is why I judge this low rather than medium. Repair: apply plain_thread_id in locate before walking.

4. LOW (correctness) — effort_token (adapters.rs ~190) accepts '-', '_', '.' and ':' as the FIRST character; seat-record.v2's effort pattern is ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*$. A harness echoing e.g. '_high' would be journaled by the fold and then refuse the entire journal at export_ndjson/verify_export — an unexportable run rather than a value clamped at the boundary. This is exactly the pre-existing model_token vs model-pattern gap (identical char set, identical leading-char looseness), so it is consistent with the repo's own idiom and not a regression this change introduced; I record it because v2 is a new contract and effort is a new field, so the mismatch is newly minted for this axis.

5. INFO — invoke_dsh_with (adapters.rs ~1486) splits --effort out of the argv and discards it. This is deliberate and documented: forwarding it would need the headless-profile change decision 0035 explicitly leaves unruled, and the task forbids widening the dsh profile. So a dsh effort pin is required by compilation, moves the bundle digest, and applies nothing. The view does make it visible ('pinned high · applied not reported'), but no doctor advisory says the pin is inert. In scope as commissioned; noted so it is on the record rather than discovered later.

Nothing here is a security finding at high or critical, so no security-hold.

1. Codex thread locator resolved once at `thread.started` and cached the miss. Announcing a thread and filing its rollout are two writes with no promised order, so a seat that won the race reported `not reported` for its whole life — dsh's sentinel on the one harness that does echo effort, collapsing the distinction ruling 3 rests on. `resolve()` is now retried while it has not succeeded, and the conformance shim files its rollout AFTER announcing the thread so the ordering is held by the gate. Verified it trips: removing the retry fails `conformance_across_all_builtin_adapters` (confirmed by temporary revert, then restored).

2. Security: `find_codex_thread` matched `name.contains(thread_id)` on an id arriving unvalidated from the harness stream. `locate` now applies `plain_thread_id` (the clamp the resume argv already used), and matching is whole-token — bounded at both ends by a non-alphanumeric — so a fragment cannot claim a longer id's file. New test `a_thread_id_that_is_not_one_locates_nothing_and_a_fragment_claims_no_file` trips both halves (`0199`, `199mine`, `0199min`, `99mi`; `../../etc`, `-flag`, `thread id`, `a/b`, 129 chars).

3. `effort_token` admitted a leading `-`/`_`/`.`/`:` where seat-record.v2's `effort` pattern requires a leading alphanumeric — a `_high` echo would be journaled and then refuse the run's whole export. The clamp is now v2's pattern exactly; the existing clamp test gains the refused leading characters plus an assertion that everything the clamp admits satisfies the contract pattern. docs/guides/driver-authoring.md states the shape and why it is clamped at the boundary.

4. Ruling 2's binding on 'every readout that labels the field': `brokkr inspect` printed a bare `model` column with no qualifier. Its seats block now carries `model is the provider's claim, not proof · effort is configuration`, matching the tui's `(claimed)` and the guide's sentence; both render goldens updated. `brokkr costs` is left as-is deliberately — it is the machine JSON join surface for LaneTally, where a prose qualifier would corrupt the record, and it already carries the wording as a source comment.

Reviewed bbd01f4..45357f4 (2 commits, 76 files) against decision 0035's seven enforcement bindings. Applied no fixes.

WHAT I VERIFIED GREEN
- Frozen surfaces untouched: zero diff on contracts/seat-record.v1.schema.json and its brokkr-store copy, contracts/driver-protocol.v1.schema.json, policy/, reference/. No journal row or evaluator fixture touched.
- v2 is v1 plus `effort` and `reasoning_output_tokens` on all three record shapes, closed (additionalProperties:false), 0031's two sentinels reused, effort described as CONFIGURATION throughout. The contracts/ and brokkr-store/ copies are byte-identical (cmp), and the embedded-copy test now pins both.
- Version dispatch is fail-closed: unparseable, absent, or pre-boundary `engine` on the run/started manifest reads under v1 (the stricter contract); the cache_read<=input invariant is generalised to reasoning<=output.
- Conformance covers all four built-ins including the absence/sentinel cases: codex per-turn effort read from the thread record (not the stream, not the pin) plus cache_write_input_tokens->cache_write_tokens and per-turn reasoning; claude per-turn effort with reasoning present ONLY on the result and asserted absent on every turn; dsh `not reported` on every checkpoint with no reasoning anywhere; exec `not applicable`.
- The compile refusal names both axes in one message with the repair, with tests that trip it (model-pinned-but-effort-unpinned alone, five malformed spellings, exec exempt, each site named exactly twice); `brokkr doctor --bundle` exposes it with its own test.
- View keeps pin and applied as two cells, fills neither from the other, and reasoning never enters total_tokens. Docs carry the full sum-rule table and ruling 2's sentence verbatim, mirrored in `brokkr inspect` and the tui.
- SECURITY (severity: none). Effort tokens are clamped to exactly v2's pattern AT the driver boundary before journaling, so no unclamped harness echo can poison an append-only journal or cost a run its export. `codex_effort_config` interpolates into `model_reasoning_effort="..."` but the value is charset-clamped (no quote, backslash or space) and passed as argv with no shell, so there is no config or command injection. The codex thread id is clamped with `plain_thread_id` before it selects a file and matched as a whole token, the walk is depth-bounded, and `../../etc`, `a/b`, `-flag` and over-long ids are all covered by tests. Result-object `effort`/`model` are overwritten by the driver, so a seat cannot forge its own hire. Nothing weakens existing fail-closed behavior. Two accepted trust boundaries are worth naming but are not findings: the contract version is selected from the journal's own `engine` string (inherent to ruling 7's wording, and v2 is a strict superset so the leniency window is one optional field), and the codex echo comes from a file the seat's own user can write with last-line-wins (the same boundary `model` already has, and ruling 2 already declines to call such a value proof).
- GATE, run by me in this worktree: `cargo test --workspace` green, 0 failures across every binary and doc-test. EXACT COVERAGE, which the verify seat could not run, I did run: `cargo +nightly llvm-cov --workspace --all-features --locked --branch` then the LCOV reduction the gate script uses -- lines 15771/15771, branches 2394/2394, functions 1481/1481, literal 100% on all three. 42 production files in the report, no test-harness leak, no `coverage(off)` attributes.
- `claude --help` on the installed CLI confirms `--effort <level>` is native with exactly the vocabulary adapters/claude.json declares (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) -- the highest-impact assumption in the change, since 10+ shipped bundles now pass it.

RESIDUAL FINDINGS (none fixed; max severity low)
1. LOW (efficiency/robustness) crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs, `CodexThreadEcho::effort()`: reads the ENTIRE codex rollout with `fs::read_to_string` on every `turn.completed`, only to take the last matching line. A rollout holds full model output and tool results and brokkr does not control its size. A 150-turn codex seat over a 50 MB rollout does ~7 GB of reads and re-allocates a 50 MB buffer per turn. Every other value crossing this boundary is bounded; this read is not. Reading a bounded tail would give the same answer.
2. LOW (test coverage) crates/brokkr-cli/tests/driver_conformance.rs: neither the dsh nor the codex conformance argv carries `--effort`, so no end-to-end test proves the dsh arm strips the pin before the spawn -- yet recipes/night-shift and recipes/wager-harness-dsh now SHIP dsh seats with `--effort medium` in their argv. I read `invoke_dsh_with` and the shadowed `passthrough` binding is correct and `split_effort` is well unit-tested, so this is a proof gap rather than a defect; if the strip regressed, two shipped recipes would fail at spawn with no test catching it.
3. LOW (judgment, for the operator) recipes/wager-harness: the codex seat now emits `-c model_reasoning_effort="medium"`, which OVERRIDES whatever ~/.codex/config.toml sets rather than inheriting it. Decision 0035's own context records a codex seat (run the-seat-record-is-a-contract-th-fab25c33) served at xhigh. If the operator's effective codex default was xhigh, this pin quietly downgrades the wager's codex lane and makes new wager runs non-comparable to recorded ones -- the exact comparability problem the decision exists to fix. I could not read ~/.codex/config.toml or run `codex exec --help` from this sandbox to confirm codex's effective default, so this needs the operator's eye rather than a code change.
4. INFO (doc/code) crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle.rs `command_pins_effort`: its comment says a level is "never a path", but the shared `concrete` predicate admits `/`, so `--effort levels/high` compiles. In practice the lint checks SHAPE and not vocabulary by design (`--effort banana` passes too, because no adapter is in hand at that point) and any bad level is refused loudly by the harness at spawn, so this is the comment overreaching rather than a hole in the refusal.
5. INFO (already recorded by the implementer, restated so the table sees it): a dsh effort pin is required by compilation and applies nothing -- it is split out of the argv and discarded, moving only the bundle digest. Forwarding it needs the headless-profile change decision 0035 deliberately leaves unruled, and commit 45357f4 records this deliberately. Noting only that an operator reading `--effort medium` on a shipped dsh seat could reasonably believe the lane is configured.
6. INFO: `brokkr costs` carries ruling 2's wording only as a source comment. Its output is pure JSON with no human label, so there is nothing to mirror onto and prose would corrupt a machine join surface -- the right call, recorded for the table.

Nothing here approaches the medium bar and nothing is a security residual. The commission is met in full: all seven bindings, the full gate, and exact coverage at literal 100%.
